record.paper_title: Some open problems in Banach space theory
record.original_question: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space. Do there exist a constant C and an exponent p in {1, 2, ∞} such that, for every positive integer n, there is a subspace Y_n of X and a bounded projection P_n from X onto Y_n with Banach-Mazur distance d(Y_n, ℓ_pⁿ) at most C and operator norm ∥P_n∥ at most C?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Recall that for a positive integer $n$ and $p \in \{1, 2, \infty\}$, the space $\ell_p^n$ denotes $\mathbb{R}^n$ (or $\mathbb{C}^n$) endowed with the norm $\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_p = \big(\sum_{i=1}^n |x_i|^p\big)^{1/p}$ for $p \in \{1,2\}$ and $\|(x_1,\dots,x_n)\|_\infty = \max_i |x_i|$ for $p = \infty$. The Banach–Mazur distance between two isomorphic Banach spaces $E$ and $F$ is
$$d(E,F) = \inf\{\|T\|\cdot\|T^{-1}\| : T : E \to F \text{ is a linear isomorphism}\}.$$
A bounded projection $P : X \to Y$ from a Banach space $X$ onto a closed subspace $Y \subseteq X$ is a bounded linear operator with $P^2 = P$ and $P(X) = Y$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: For every infinite-dimensional Banach space $X$, there exist a constant $C > 0$ and an exponent $p \in \{1, 2, \infty\}$ such that for every positive integer $n$ there is a closed subspace $Y_n \subseteq X$ and a bounded projection $P_n : X \to Y_n$ satisfying
$$d(Y_n, \ell_p^n) \le C \quad \text{and} \quad \|P_n\| \le C.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every infinite-dimensional Banach space contains uniformly complemented copies of ℓ_p^n for some fixed p ∈ {1, 2, ∞} is a long-standing open problem in Banach space theory. Searches surface only partial/conditional results (e.g., uniform factorization of ℓ_p^n inclusions through X under certain non-factorization hypotheses on operators into L_p), and surveys on complemented subspaces continue to list this circle of questions as unresolved. No source verifying a full solution was found.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on the Complemented Subspace Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing complemented subspaces problems in Banach spaces, none of which resolves the uniform ℓ_p^n complementation question for general infinite-dimensional X.
status_evidence.claim: The complemented-subspace circle of problems concerning uniform copies of ℓ_p^n in arbitrary infinite-dimensional Banach spaces remains a central open area.

status_evidence.title: Combinatorics in Banach space theory — Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Problem set listing classical open questions in Banach space theory, including those on uniformly complemented finite-dimensional subspaces.
status_evidence.claim: The uniform ℓ_p^n complementation question is still posed as an open problem in current problem lists.
